filename: Recommendations for comprehensive and independent evaluation of machine learning-based Earth system models_.pdf
title: Recommendations for Comprehensive and Independent Evaluation of Machine Learning-Based Earth System Models
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review article providing recommendations and benchmark menus for evaluating ML-based Earth system models. Although small demonstrative simulation outputs are archived on Zenodo, it does not release a benchmark training/evaluation dataset testbed for parameterizations.
pain_points: ML models often fail to explicitly enforce physical conservation laws (mass, momentum, energy).
Evaluating out-of-sample generalization is challenging because the historical instrumental record is short, stationary, and only a single realization of climate history.
Spectral damping at high wavenumbers leads to an effective resolution in ML models that is much coarser than their nominal grid spacing.
Unlike physics-based models, monolithic ML models cannot easily have individual physical components activated or deactivated without complete retraining.

Pre-trained ML models internalize realistic geographic topography and land-sea contrasts, making standardized idealized tests (e.g., zonally symmetric or flat aquaplanets) difficult to apply directly.
Risk of metric hacking and cherry-picking if evaluations are not standardized across a comprehensive suite of physical metrics.
extraction_notes: The paper outlines five major recommendations for evaluating ML-based ESMs (benchmarking toolkits, physical sanity checks, emergent constraints, idealized dynamical test cases, and multi-model intercomparisons). Figures 1 and 2 showcase demonstrative runs using ACE and SFNO with data deposited on Zenodo.
